title: Chiral bosonic mean-field Ansatz and spin dynamics in spin-1 Kitaev magnets
authors: Daiki Sasamoto, Arnaud Ralko, Jaime Merino, Joji Nasu
abstract: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic system for realizing quantum spin liquids, but its higher-spin extensions are not exactly solvable, and their spin dynamics is less well understood than in the spin-1/2 case. In this work, we reexamine a previously introduced triplet-pairing $φ_t = π/2$ phase pattern for the antiferromagnetic $S = 1$ Kitaev model and extend the analysis to weak symmetric off-diagonal exchanges $Γ$ and $Γ'$. Using a bond-operator formulation of Schwinger-boson mean-field theory, we calculate the dynamical spin structure factor for the triplet 0-flux and triplet $π/2$-flux Ansätze with a spin-correlation scheme appropriate for Kitaev interactions. In the pure Kitaev limit, the $π/2$-flux Ansatz yields a flatter spectrum than the 0-flux Ansatz. The real-space spin correlations show that the $π/2$-flux Ansatz suppresses longer-distance correlations more strongly than the 0-flux Ansatz, yielding a correlation pattern closer to the short-ranged form expected in the Kitaev limit. This comparison shows that the flatness of $S(\boldsymbol{q}, ω)$ is tied to short-ranged spin correlations and is therefore an important consistency check, although it is not, by itself, a diagnostic of time-reversal-symmetry breaking. We then study weak off-diagonal exchanges along $Γ' = Γ$ near the pure Kitaev limit, taking the same-sign relation from analyses of candidate spin-1 Kitaev materials. Gapped solutions are obtained within the constrained $π/2$-flux manifold, and the spectra share the qualitative energy- and momentum-space features found by finite-size exact diagonalization. Taken together, these results support the triplet $π/2$-flux chiral bosonic Ansatz as a useful mean-field description of spin dynamics near the antiferromagnetic $S = 1$ Kitaev limit with weak off-diagonal exchanges.
summary: This work investigates the spin dynamics of the $S=1$ Kitaev magnet using Schwinger-boson mean-field theory. By comparing the 0-flux and $\pi/2$-flux Ansätze, the authors demonstrate that the chiral $\pi/2$-flux Ansatz provides a robust description, particularly near the pure Kitaev limit with weak perturbations. This supports the use of chiral bosonic methods for modeling spin liquid behavior in higher-spin systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to understand the complex spin dynamics in higher-spin ($S=1$) Kitaev magnets, which are not exactly solvable, by comparing different mean-field descriptions.
main_result: The triplet $\pi/2$-flux chiral bosonic Ansatz is supported as a useful mean-field description, showing that this flux pattern yields a flatter spectrum and better captures short-range correlations compared to the 0-flux Ansatz.
method: The analysis employs Schwinger-boson mean-field theory (SBMFT) using a bond-operator formulation to calculate the dynamical spin structure factor.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1 Kitaev model on the honeycomb lattice, generalized to include weak symmetric off-diagonal exchanges ($\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$).
key_observables: Dynamical spin structure factor $S( oldsymbol{q}, \omega)$, real-space spin correlations, and spectral flatness.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the pure Kitaev limit and weak perturbations along the line $\Gamma' = \Gamma$.
main_assumptions: The study relies on the triplet 0-flux and $\pi/2$-flux Ansätze within the SBMFT framework, and spectral flatness is noted as a consistency check, not a definitive diagnostic of chirality.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the context suggests figures comparing spectral features and correlation functions between different flux Ansätze.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the pure Kitaev limit by comparing the 0-flux and $\pi/2$-flux Ansätze. It then extends the analysis to weak off-diagonal exchanges ($\Gamma, \Gamma'$) and confirms the utility of the $\pi/2$-flux Ansatz by comparing results to finite-size exact diagonalization.
why_interesting: The detailed study of spin dynamics and the comparison of different mean-field Ansätze provide valuable insights into the nature of quantum spin liquid ground states, which is central to understanding strongly correlated magnetic materials.

Panels (a) and (b) show the 0-flux and π/2-flux Ansätze, respectively. The spectra are plotted along the path connecting the high-symmetry points indicated in Fig. 1. The color scale, common to both panels, indicates the intensity of S (q, ω), and the broadening parameter is set to δ/|K| = 0.01.

Panels (d)–(f) show the corresponding energy dependence at the representative high-symmetry momenta K, Γ, M, and Γ′.
